creator.f.def_formula_guide:
📘 How to use Definition Formulas

Formulas are used to calculate the final value of this definition code. Write expressions according to the rules below:

1 · Reference other definitions

Type the code name (e.g., atk) to get that definition's final value. Add prefixes to target specific layers:

  • code — final value of code
  • base.code — base layer only
  • bonus.code — bonus layer only
  • acalc.code — auxiliary calculation layer
  • current.code — current value of the resource (used in regen formulas)
  • max.code — configured maximum of the resource (used in regen formulas)
  • time — the time amount in the current regeneration unit (used in regen formulas)
  • bcalc.code — isolated calculation (sandbox), does not share variables with the main formula
  • bcalc.(expression) — isolated calculation with direct expression, e.g., bcalc.(base.atk * 2 + bonus.atk)
2 · Numbers, Strings & Booleans
  • 42 — integer
  • 3.14 — float
  • "text" or 'text' — string (used in if/else)
  • true / false — boolean values
3 · Operators & Comparisons

+ - * / — add, subtract, multiply, divide; % — percentage (e.g., + 50%). Comparisons: == != < <= > >=; logical operators: && (AND) / || (OR).

4 · Grouping with Parentheses

Use ( ) to group sub-expressions and control evaluation order:

  • (base.atk + bonus.atk) * 2 — multiply after addition
  • (a && b) || (c && d) — combine multiple conditions
5 · Conditionals

Ternary: condition ? true : false. Condition block: if(condition) { ... } else { ... }; add branches using elif(...) or else if(...).

6 · Math & Trigonometry
  • sin() cos() tan() cot() — trigonometry
  • square() root() abs() — power, square root, absolute value
  • pow(base, exp) — exponentiation (base raised to exp)
  • log(x) — natural logarithm
  • exp(x) — e raised to the power of x
  • mod(x, y) — modulo (remainder)
  • lerp(a, b, t) — linear interpolation
  • min() max() clamp(x, min, max) — minimum, maximum, value clamp
  • round() floor() ceil() — rounding functions
7 · RNG & Probability (Game/TRPG)
  • rand(min, max) — random float in range [min, max]
  • chance(percent) — returns true with percent% probability
  • dice(n, d) — roll n dice with d sides each (sum of values 1-d per die)
8 · Type Casting & Utilities
  • coalesce(val1, val2, ...) — returns first non-null/non-empty value
  • toInt(val) — cast to integer
  • toFloat(val) — cast to float
9 · Operator Precedence

From highest to lowest precedence: ( ) → functions → * / % → + - → < <= > >= → == != → && → || → ? : → if/else

10 · Examples
  • hp → base.hp + bonus.hp
  • dmg → (base.atk * 1.5 + bonus.atk) * (crit ? 2 : 1)
  • def2 → max(base.def, acalc.def) + 100
  • status → if(base.mp >= 50) { "Sufficient Mana" } else { "Insufficient Mana" }
  • hp_lerp → lerp(base.hp, max.hp, 0.5) — HP between base and max value
  • mana_regen → rand(5, 10) * time — random regen 5-10 per time unit
  • crit → chance(25) ? damage * 2 : damage — 25% critical hit
  • xp_bonus → dice(2, 6) — bonus XP from rolling 2d6
  • rank → if(score>=90) { "S" } elif(score>=70) { "A" } else { "B" }
11 · Tips & Notes
  • Whitespace does not affect calculation results; use it for readability
  • Strings returned inside if/else must be wrapped in double or single quotes
  • If referenced code does not exist, it defaults to 0
  • You can nest if/else and ? : as needed

noscript.tools: JavaScript must be enabled in your browser to use this feature.
note.1: When importing a .txt file, the content must follow this structure:
note.2:
1. STRUCTURE TAGS 
 <>...</>; → Title (novel title)
 <;info>; ... <;/info>; → Novel information (author, description, genres, etc.)
[ ... ] → Character list
<;list>; ... <;/list>; → Chapter list
{ ... } → Chapter content
 • → System checker / marker (do not delete; chapter content must be inside this marker)
note.3:
2. MANDATORY RULES
Do not modify, delete, or change any MDT tags.
All content inside the file must maintain its original structure.
System tags are mandatory.
If formatted incorrectly, the tool may fail to read the content.
note.4:
3. FILE REQUIREMENT
The tool runs completely offline.
Users must prepare correctly formatted .txt files themselves.
The tool only supports files converted according to MDT standards.
note.5:
4. DISCLAIMER
If file errors occur due to incorrect formatting edits, the tool bears no responsibility.
The tool does not guarantee reading files from non-MDT compliant sources.
Only recommended to use tool-generated files or self-designed files following spec.
